The coarse recitation of eighty-one words is manifested through reflection, and from that the reflection is completed as one.
So long that word is spoken, not bound by sleep-verb rule, but empowered by the great reflection of eighty-one words.
The coarse means is indeed this supreme means, a dissolution made by measure, with half-measures nine and nine in four and four.
Thus in the fingers thirty-six and eighty-one words arise; when a finger is divided by a ninth part, ninth portions result.
The Vedas, another half-measure, twice-four-six multiplied, three; thus light goes through two sets of four finger-hole portions.
Long, prolated, gradually two-three multiplied half; from that also consonant, ksha is three half-measures, measured, with intervals between.
When its resting half-measure is counted, in that finger half by a third part, then half-measure occurs before and again.
Ksha is the self of all combination-grasping, but all-pervading, ruler and share of all letter arising from beginning to end and junctions.
Thus in the thirty-six course letters arise; in cruel or gentle result, in reverse from ha until the last.
Heart-a at the twelfth end, ha-letter; knowers know this as i-self nondual, which is rest in the self of light.
By nondivision of Shiva and Shakti, this eighty-one measure circulates in seventy-two fingers by doubling.
Subtle arising is threefold, supreme arising is twofold; now coarse arising of letters is spoken by the teacher.
Some say eight vargas rise by half a watch each day, with decrease and increase at night, while others disagree.
This varga rise, moving by half a watch day and night, is counted as thirteen hundred fifty breaths.
Indeed, one and a half transitions occur per varga in day and night, and four hundred twenty-seven rise.
For the nine vargas, one hundred breaths are assigned, and a one-third transition per varga is stated.
In the union of day and night, the gross varga rise, counted in hundreds, is called by this ocean-like name.
Each letter has two hundred sixteen breaths, thus also at night and outside.
There, one hundred eight raudra and shakta are counted, and rudra and shakti remain indivisible in yamala union.
In day-night division, sight, fire, water, moon, and recitation with a fifth part nadi are remembered as outside letter rise.
Thus this fifty-verse discussion of letters is completed; some call it one less, and we declare their opinion.
Four vedas, fifth part less, and one each of four halves are more in a letter, doubled and indivisible in day and night.
This gross letter rise was before declared as subtle.
Thus the time principle is declared, established by scripture, oral tradition, and experience.
